Team / Ethan — attached is our sizing recommendation ("redwood_gpu_sizing_recs.pdf"). Summary below.

Key inputs we used (from your sheet + telemetry):
- Current steady-state: 8 GPUs, average sustained QPS (chat) 120, avg tokens/req 1.2k, 95% utilization on reserved pool at peak windows.
- Forecast: 6-month peak QPS up to 185 (55% growth), tokens/req median 1.8k; burst windows up to 260 QPS.
- SLO target: 99th-pctl token gen latency < 300ms for chat.

Our recommended renewal upsell (cost/ops tradeoff):
Option A — Conservative (recommended for predictable SLO):
- Add 4 GPUs to reserved pool (total 12 GPUs).
- Config: dedicated 12-GPU pool with autoscale headroom to 16 GPUs for bursts (billing on committed+burst hours).
- Tokens/sec SLA: guaranteed baseline 420k tokens/sec (measured as sustained 5m window); burst tolerance to 600k tokens/sec for 30m/day before fallback policies.

Option B — Aggressive (lower latency tail, higher commit):
- Commit to 16 GPUs reserved (adds 8).
- SLA baseline 560k tokens/sec; burst to 800k tokens/sec.

Operational notes:
- With Option A we project 99th-pctl under 300ms in 95% of peak windows; 99th tail during extreme bursts will be mitigated by autoscale to 16 GPUs.
- Option B gives comfortable headroom, reduces autoscale triggers, and is recommended if StellarSol wants to remove burst billing variability.

Contract/term considerations (Ben):
- We'll add explicit tokens/sec baseline in the Dedicated Addendum and define burst windows + fair use.
- Suggested renewal term: 12-month committed pool with quarterly telemetry reviews and two 1-month symmetric ramp windows.

Attachments: sizing + a short MCP-term-summary.docx with changes called out.

Happy to run a 48-hour stress run on a mirror environment before final commit — ping us preferred test dates.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
